title: Fugaro recipe
description: .fugaro/recipes/<name>.yaml, or fugaro/recipes/<name>.yaml in the runs bucket. See docs/recipes.md. At most 16 KiB; anchors, aliases, tags, repeated keys and extra documents are refused.

name.description: Must equal the file name (repository) or the object name (project).

description.$comment: The pattern refuses C0, DEL, C1 and the BMP format characters and line separators the Go parser refuses (recipe.hasControlChar); the parser is stricter (it also refuses the astral format characters). maxLength here counts Unicode characters (the JSON Schema spec); the Go parser's 200-byte limit (recipe.MaxDescription) is stricter for any multi-byte character, so this schema accepts some strings the parser refuses.

use_when.$comment: maxLength here counts Unicode characters (the JSON Schema spec); the Go parser's 300-byte limit (recipe.MaxUseWhen) is stricter for any multi-byte character, so this schema accepts some strings the parser refuses. The pattern matches the BMP part of the parser's control-character, format-character and line-separator refusal.

by_level.description: The recipe's one conditional: the roles: mapping the recipe resolves at a given rigor level, which replaces roles: at that level (recipe.RolesFor). A level written with an empty roles block resolves to no mapping. Nothing else is conditioned: the per-run cap is the level's own and the loop's shape is the recipe's, so any other key is refused. No run applies the block yet: the runner and the level resolver both apply the recipe's own roles: once, at bootstrap, before the run's level is known, so a recipe that writes it runs on its top-level roles: at every level.

allOf.$comment: outputs: is mode: artifact's own block: a run that opens a pull request delivers its diff, not a file set (recipe.Parse refuses the block in the other two modes, whatever the mode key's value).

A plan, render or diagnose step is mode: artifact's own shape too: recipe.Parse refuses any of them in the other two modes with '<kind> is only for mode: artifact' (order), whatever the mode key's value. The steps oneOf above has to list artifactSteps as one alternative for an artifact recipe to have any shape at all, and without this branch that alternative admits [render] (or [diagnose]) under mode: implement — which Go refuses (testdata/recipe/invalid/render-implement.yaml, and its mirror in this schema's own corpus test).

A registered step kind is its mode's own shape: recipe.Parse refuses ab_judge in every other mode with 'ab_judge is a step of mode: evaluate, not of mode: <mode>' (order, orderArtifact), so the steps oneOf's alternative for it must not admit an implement, review or artifact recipe. An artifact recipe is refused by this branch too, and by mode: artifact's own branch above, which is the shape it already had.

reviewer.description: The reviewer role runs on the coder's model and output limit.

coder.description: The coder role runs on the reviewer's (strong) model.

globs.description: The artifact paths to upload, relative to the checkout root. An absolute glob, or one with a .. path element, is refused (recipe.Parse): a recipe may never name a file outside the run's own tree.

max_files.description: How many artifacts the run may upload; absent means 8 (recipe.DefaultOutputFiles).

max_bytes.description: The most ONE artifact may hold; absent means 256 MiB (recipe.DefaultOutputBytes). A written 0 is refused, not read as the default.

max_total_bytes.description: The most the WHOLE SET may hold; absent means 2 GiB (recipe.DefaultOutputTotalBytes). The runner stages a second copy of the set beside the render's originals, so this is what the workflow's resources.memory must hold twice over (docs/artifact-runs/spec.md §5.2).

probe.description: Whether commands.probe runs on what was rendered; absent means none.

artifactSteps.description: A mode: artifact recipe's steps: one render or one diagnose, optionally led by one plan (recipe.Parse's orderArtifact). A diagnose step delivers the two files the recipe's outputs block names, so it stands where a render stands and never beside one.

diagnose.description: The cloud tier of `fugaro troubleshoot`'s own step (recipe.StepDiagnose, docs/troubleshoot-cloud D2402): one model stage reads the evidence a launcher left under the run's own prefix and writes the two files the recipe's outputs block names — out/diagnosis.md and out/diagnosis.json in the catalog's troubleshoot. It takes no options, like digest and render, and recipe.Parse refuses it anywhere but alone or after one plan in a mode: artifact recipe, at most once. The stage's per-call output bound is the recipe's (recipe.TroubleshootReviewerMaxOutput, which the runner applies to the slot the stage's own call reads). recipe.TroubleshootMaxTurns is D2407's turn bound written down and read by nothing: the stage's call has no turn knob, so a cloud diagnosis is bounded by that per-call reservation, the run's own lease and the stage's timeout.

digest.description: The report run's deterministic first step (recipe.StepDigest): it takes no options, and recipe.Parse refuses it anywhere but first in a mode: implement recipe, at most once, and followed by exactly one review step.

commitReports.description: The commit run's deterministic first step (recipe.StepCommitReports, docs/periodic-reviews E5): the runner writes the run reports the launcher handed in into the repository and folder the project's published policy designates and commits them, naming no model. It takes no options, like digest, and recipe.Parse refuses it anywhere but first in a mode: implement recipe, at most once, and followed by exactly one review step.

reviewHandOver.description: A review step that hands the run over (recipe.Step.HandOver, the escalation's escalate recipe): the run ends at that review with the verdict recorded and no fix round after it. hand_over: false is refused (the key is simply not written), and recipe.Parse refuses the key beside bounce: first_line and on a review an adversarial step follows, neither of which this shape admits.

rebase.description: The rebase run's only step (recipe.StepRebase): the runner puts the branch on its base, hands the conflicts to one model stage, runs the workflow's tests again and pushes. recipe.Parse refuses the step anywhere but alone in a mode: implement recipe, and a recipe holding it is its own shape — the step is the whole run, so it needs no review step after it, which is why the oneOf lists it in a variant of its own.

adversarialNoBounce.description: Review level 3's step (recipe.StepAdversarial): at most once, only after the review step, and last. Absent max_rounds means the rigor mode's senior row (rigor.AdversarialDefault): 1 at poc and hotfix, 2 at startup, 3 at pro, 5 at critical. This is the shape for a recipe with no first_line step, where a bounce has nothing to bounce back to.

adversarialBounce.description: The adversarial step beside a firstLine step: bounce is optional (as it is in reviewBounce) and first_line is its only value, so a rejection runs the fix and then another first-line loop. recipe.Parse refuses the bounce when no first_line step precedes the step, which is why the oneOf pairs this def with firstLine.

evaluateSteps.description: A mode: evaluate recipe's steps: exactly one, and it is either a step kind this build registered as that mode's own (recipe.RegisterStepKind, orderEvaluate) or the core's own judge step (recipe.StepMergeJudge). The judge runs are the only ones today — ab_judge, and the core's merge_judge beside it — and the mode's rules are why: an evaluate run reads material the bucket already holds, so a step that runs a repository command or starts an agent is refused by name rather than run.

mergeJudge.description: The merge judge run's only step (recipe.StepMergeJudge, the escalation ladder's rung 3): one read-only stage reads the diff, the open findings and the fundamentals checklist the launcher left under the run's prefix, and answers merge with follow-ups or blocked. It carries no keys, and it is not a registered kind — the code behind it is this tree's (internal/runner/mergejudge.go), not the Subscription Edition's. The verdict can only veto: the run checks no branch out, pushes nothing and opens no pull request.

abJudge.description: The judge run's only step (recipe.StepKind ab_judge, registered by ee/ab through ee/register): the runner hands the run's registered step its own prefix and one tool-less model call per pass, and the step judges each pair in the manifest the launcher wrote, blind, twice with the order swapped. It carries no keys — there is nothing to configure here: what the judge reads and what it writes are the manifest's and the pair's (D552, D559).
